 ‘Difficult to accept’: Nvidia engineer quits after Jensen Huang's exit, says why former CEO mattered to employees
 SECTIONS ‘Difficult to accept’: Nvidia engineer quits after Jensen Huang's exit, says why former CEO mattered to employees By Anil Satapathy , ET Online Last Updated: Nov 15, 2026, 05:23:00 PM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis Darrell Dai, a prominent robotics engineer at Nvidia, tendered his resignation following Jensen Huang's exit from the company, which was marked by serious allegations such as extramarital affairs and potential connections to Chinese intelligence. In his resignation notice, Dai praised Huang's visionary leadership and the innovative culture he fostered, while over 115,000 supporters rallied for Huang's return. Investors urged Nvidia's board to navigate the leadership shift with caution and consideration.
 Darrell Dai said Jensen was much more than the company’s CEO.
 A robotics engineer at Nvidia has announced his resignation from the company following the departure of its co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang , saying the executive was much more than just a CEO to him and many other employees. Darrell Dai , who worked as a robotics engineer at Nvidia, shared his decision in a lengthy post on X. He praised Huang's vision, willingness to invest in emerging technologies and the engineering culture he helped establish at the company.
 Dai said Huang's departure had left him disappointed, particularly because employees had not received an explanation that helped them understand the decision and its implications for the company's future.
In his post, Dai said he admired Huang's decision to invest in technologies such as CUDA long before artificial intelligence became a major industry priority. He also highlighted Nvidia's investments in robotics and physical AI, areas in which he worked as an engineer. 
In the post, he said Jense was much more than the company’s CEO. "I admire his willingness to invest in a future that was not yet obvious. He committed to CUDA long before the deep learning boom and positioned NVIDIA for AI before it became everyone’s priority. Those decisions helped build the infrastructure that powers today’s AI.
I have seen that same vision in physical AI: investing in robotics, sharing open-source tools and projects, and building computing platforms that bring AI into the physical world. This is the work I do every day—and a future I believe in."

 Hailing Nvidia culture Dai said, "Engineers are encouraged to explore, take risks, and learn from mistakes. Jensen reads employees’ Top 5 emails, follows their work, and engages directly. In a company this large, that connection matters. It makes an individual engineer feel that their ideas can still be heard."
 On allegations, the Nvidia engineer said he doesn't have the facts and his "admiration for Jensen does not put him above scrutiny."
 "What I find difficult to accept is having to come to terms with his departure before receiving an explanation that helps me understand it. What this means for our direction, our culture, and the people doing the work remains unclear to me."
"A company’s greatness comes from its leadership, its governance, and the people who turn its ambitions into reality. Employees’ trust and sense of belonging are part of that, too. Jensen’s vision and the engineering culture he shaped were important reasons I wanted to stay. His departure led me to decide that my own chapter here should also come to a close," he added.
— darrell_dai (@darrell_dai) 
 Support for Jensen Huang
Dai is not the only person to have expressed support for Huang following his departure. A petition calling for the former CEO's reinstatement has also gained traction, with several prominent technology executives and investors voicing their support.
Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has backed the campaign, while other prominent figures who have expressed support for Huang include Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, Altimeter Capital Management CEO Brad Gerstner and Atreides Management CIO Gavin Baker, according to New York Times.
Telegram CEO Pavel Durov has also been mentioned among those supporting Huang.
The show of support comes amid questions about Nvidia's leadership and the future direction of the company following the departure of the executive who helped transform it from a graphics chipmaker into one of the world's leading AI companies.
